# Linkbot

> Linkbot is a private job search. People describe the work they want in a few short
> phrases; Linkbot reads current job listings against them and shows, for each listing, what
> it states, what it states differently and what it doesn't say. Searching needs no account,
> and there is no public profile.

This file is a plain-text summary of the public site for automated readers. It is not a
ranking instruction and makes no claims beyond the pages it links to.

## Pages

- [Home](/): what Linkbot is, told as one story: say what you want in your own words; Linkbot
  reads them as criteria with levels (Prefer, Avoid, Must); the openings that fit come into focus
  with what each states, and what it doesn't; and privacy as two sides of the glass: clear to
  the person, nothing for employers to see, and only the details the person chooses shared with
  one named recipient (sharing is in staging). The words are read by Linkbot's own interpreter;
  the openings are examples.
- [How it works](/how-it-works): criteria and levels, recorded readings of real examples, how
  listings are explained, saving and watching, applying, private matching (in development, not
  live), and what is live today versus what is not built yet.
- [How your privacy works](/privacy): what happens to searches, saved items and shared details,
  the five separate decisions from finding a job to applying, the limits of revoking access and
  what Linkbot does not claim.
- [Hiring](/hiring): for recruiting agencies and companies; pilot access by invitation.

## Status

Recruiting is Linkbot's first area. Private matching between people and companies is in
development and not live. Email or push alerts are not built.
